****Job Description:****
**Are you ready to steer quality operations for a global leader in vertical flight?**
Airbus Helicopters is seeking a visionary, results-oriented
**Site Quality Director**
to lead our site-level Quality Management System (QMS) and daily operational integrity. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, you will serve as the operational anchor for aviation safety, manufacturing excellence, and regulatory compliance across FAA, EASA, TCCA, and AS9100 standards.
  
  
In this high-visibility leadership role, you will direct a team of quality professionals across logistics, assembly, component repair, and final conformity. We are looking for a strategic change-maker who can embed a "First Time Right" mindset, harmonize site practices with global Airbus standards, and bridge the gap between engineering, regulatory bodies, and frontline operations.
  
  
**Your working environment:**
On the eastern border of Mississippi you’ll find Columbus, home to our Helicopter manufacturing and assembly lines and Center of Excellence for the entire North America region. It’s here that we produce the UH-72A Lakota Helicopters for the U.S. Army in addition to the H-125 aircraft for civil and commercial customers.
  
  
**How we care for you:**

* Financial Rewards: Competitive base salary, incentive compensation which may include profit sharing schemes, retirement savings plan and the ability to participate in an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (“ESOP”)
* Work/Life Balance: Paid time off including personal time, holidays and a generous paid parental leave program.
* Health & Welfare: Comprehensive insurance coverage including medical (traditional and high-deductible health plans), prescription, dental, vision, life, disability, Employee Assistance Plan (“EAP”) and other supplemental benefit coverages.
* Individual Development: Upskilling and development opportunities through our global Leadership University, including unlimited access to 10,000+ e-learning courses focusing on ways to develop your employability, certifications, career path as well as the opportunity to participate in accelerated development programmes and both national and international mobility.

**Your Challenges:**

* Sustain Regulatory & Quality Certifications: Maintain, uphold, and expand site compliance for FAA, EASA, and TCCA repair station and production certificates, certified personnel, and AS9100 QMS credentials.
* Drive Executive QMS Governance: Administer the site Quality Management System, collaborating directly with the Executive Committee to embed strategic quality objectives into the business planning cycle.
* Standardize Operational Inspections: Supervise and enforce rigorous inspection standards across supply chain, logistics, receiving, in-process assembly, quality gates, and final aircraft conformity for components, aerostructures, and rotorcraft.
* Mitigate Quality Escapes & Risk: Identify and eliminate operational and airworthiness risks to safeguard customer flight safety, business continuity, delivery schedules, and operating costs.
* Lead and Develop Personnel: Directly manage, mentor, and evaluate a team of 3-5 exempt supervisors/engineers and 10-25 non-exempt inspectors, directing career progression, staffing, and technical competence.
* Establish & Track SQCDP KPIs: Implement robust enterprise metrics tracking Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, and People (SQCDP) to systematically capture non-conformances, process capability, and customer complaints.
* Manage Financials & Quality Budget: Direct departmental budgeting, manage financial forecasts, analyze cost variances, and allocate capital for advanced measurement tools, calibration, and ergonomic work environments.
* Execute Root Cause & Corrective Action (RCCA): Drive practical problem solving (PPS), Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), and structured RCCA workflows to resolve manufacturing anomalies and prevent recurrence.
* Harmonize Global Airbus Standards: Coordinate with international Airbus Helicopters facilities to standardize quality procedures, digital architectures, and enterprise systems (including SAP, MES, and non-conformance portals).
* Champion Safety and "First Time Right" Culture: Spearhead a proactive, psychological safety culture anchored by "First Time Right" execution and a robust "Speak Up / Listen Up" mindset across all shifts and departments.
* Direct Internal & External Audits: Lead preparation, execution, and reporting for internal, regulatory (FAA/EASA/TCCA), and customer audits, ensuring all corrective action milestones are closed transparently.
* Collaborate on Design & New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with design engineering and certification teams to support new product development, configuration integrity, obsolescence management, and manufacturing build cycles.
* Reduce Cost of Non-Quality (CoNQ): Lead enterprise continuous improvement, Lean, and Kaizen initiatives to eliminate scrap, minimize rework, reduce the Cost of Non-Quality, and improve delivery reliability.
* Optimize Workload & Production Flow: Coordinate with operations and program management to balance inspection staffing and shift priorities against critical flightline and customer delivery schedules.
* Oversee Technical Training & Qualifications: Build and finance comprehensive onboarding and recurrent training programs covering aviation safety, specialized processes (NDI, composites, dynamic components), and regulatory requirements.

**Your Boarding Pass:**

* Must possess a Bachelor’s Degree in Aerospace/Aviation/Industrial Engineer/Engineering related field or equivalent experience (4 years)
* Have ten (10) + years of Aerospace/Aviation Industry, Military or Quality experience and three (3) + years in a Leadership role, Civilian and/or Military
* Able to support functions in multiple areas such as repair station, manufacturing, composites, electrical/avionics Backshop, warehousing/logistics, dynamic component repair, blades and tail boom
* Knowledge of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Regulations 14 CFR Parts 21, 43 and 145 in addition the related sections for Transport Canada and EASA
* Knowledge of AS9100 Quality Requirements and Systems
* Knowledge of aircraft design, maintenance, and manufacturing processes and build cycles
* Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Access), Onbase, Orion eTechPub, Adobe Acrobat , SAP, Smartsheet, G Suite. OCE/ARAS/Bflow T.I.P.I.

**Preferred Education/Skills:**

* Master’s Degree as described above
* 12 years of Aerospace/Aviation Industry, Military or Quality experience and 3 years in a Leadership role Civilian and/or Military
* A&P License
* ASQ or CMQ certified

**Travel Required:**

* 15% Domestic and International

**Citizenship:**

* Must be a US Person under ITAR definition (U.S. Citizen, green card holder or person covered under our existing ITAR license)

**Physical Requirements:**

* Onsite or remote: 100% in Columbus, MS unless traveling
* Vision: able to see and read computer screens and other electronic equipment with screens, able to read documents, reports and engineering drawings daily. Must have correctable near and far vision if applicable.
* Hearing: able to hear to participate in conversations in person and via teleconference or phone and to hear sounds on the production floor including safety warnings or alarms. Daily
* Speaking: able to speak in conversations and meetings, deliver information and participate in communications. Daily
* Equipment Operation (personal computer, telephone, copies, fax machine, and related office equipment and using electronic identification card to enter building floors and internal doors): able to operate most office and personal electronic equipment and some tools including production tools .
* Carrying: able to carry documents, tools, drawings, electronic equipment up to 30lbs/14kgs. Daily
* Lifting: able to lift documents, tools, drawings, electronic equipment up to 30lbs/14kgs. Daily
* Pushing / Pulling: able to push and pull small office furniture and some equipment and tools. Daily
* Sitting: able to sit for long periods of time in meetings, working on the computer. Several times a week
* Squatting / Kneeling: able to squat or kneel to retrieve or replace items stored on low shelving. Daily
* Standing: able to stand for discussions in offices or on the production floor. Daily
* Travel: able to travel independently and at short notice. 15% or less yearly
* Walking (include routine walking such as to a shared printer to retrieve documents): able to walk through office and production areas including uneven surfaces. Daily
* Personal Protective Equipment required: Required PPE includes, but is not limited to, Safety Shoes, Safety Glasses, Hearing Protection, Respirators/Masks, and/or Protective Gloves as required by site and/or customer site
* Administrative position only PPE required: Steel-toed shoes are required for all shop floor visits, appropriate hearing/eye protection may also be required when visiting the shop floor.

records.description:
**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.

records.description:
**Company Overview**
Red 6 is an innovative Augmented Reality (AR) technology startup leading the way in synthetic air combat training. Our primary technology, supporting our ATARS product, enables pilots to simulate the cognitive challenges of flying while accessing realistic, scalable training in dynamic outdoor environments.
  
  
**Director of Quality**
Lead Red 6 into a scalable aerospace product organization.
  
  
Red 6 develops advanced augmented reality capabilities for aerospace and defense applications. We seek a hands-on, strategic Director of Quality to lead the next phase of our evolution into disciplined, repeatable product qualification and production. This leader will strengthen existing foundations while guiding the processes, evidence, and behaviors needed to meet customer, regulatory, safety, and aerospace industry expectations.
  
  
Success requires more than maintaining certifications. The Director will embed quality planning into product development, improve manufacturing and supplier readiness, and create a culture in which teams jointly solve problems before they become defects, delays, or compliance findings. Key results are building practical, auditable quality processes with Quality as a trusted partner across Engineering, Operations, Programs, and the supplier base.
  
  
**What You Will Lead**

* Own the enterprise Quality strategy and roadmap, scaling the Quality Management System (QMS) to match product maturity, production volume, and customer commitments.
* Maintain and continuously improve AS9100 certification and audit readiness. Lead management reviews, internal audits, corrective action effectiveness, risk based thinking, and process ownership.
* Lead ISO 45001 occupational health and safety management system maturation and certification readiness, in coordination with accountable safety and operations leaders.
* Deploy practical Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) disciplines aligned to AS9145 where applicable, including quality planning, process flow, PFMEA, control plans, measurement system analysis, first article inspection, and production readiness reviews.
* Integrate Quality into design inputs, reviews, verification and validation, configuration control, design changes, manufacturing transitions, and product release criteria.
* Establish scalable document and record controls, product pedigree, serial level traceability, inspection and test evidence, nonconformance controls, material review, CAPA, and calibration systems.
* Develop supplier qualification, surveillance, performance scorecards, supplier corrective actions, and risk based oversight of contract manufacturers and critical suppliers.
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to strengthen hardware quality, reliability, manufacturability, process validation, FOD/ESD controls, and handling of nonconforming material.
* Improve the connection between Windchill PLM, Epsilon3 MES, Unanet ERP, and existing compliance tools to support controlled, usable, auditable data across design, build, and delivery.
* Lead customer quality engagement, audits, contractual quality deliverables, and coordination with defense and aerospace stakeholders as applicable.

**LEAD A COLLABORATIVE QUALITY CULTURE**

* Build a capable Quality team with clear roles, coaching, succession planning, and cross functional influence.
* Act as a constructive partner to Engineering. Translate standards and contractual obligations into design intent, risk, and measurable acceptance criteria rather than relying on clause citations alone.
* Distinguish nonnegotiable compliance outcomes from implementation choices. Invite Engineering and Operations to co-design efficient solutions.
* Create early quality engagement in program planning and design reviews. Resolve disagreements using evidence, risk, cost, schedule, and accountable decision ownership.
* Establish shared performance measures and a regular Quality–Engineering working cadence to reduce late surprises and unproductive escalation.
* Promote a just, learning oriented culture that encourages timely issue reporting, root cause analysis, and effective preventive action.

**Qualifications Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Significant progressive aerospace or defense quality leadership experience, including building or scaling an AS9100 QMS and leading certification or surveillance audits.
* Demonstrated success moving products from prototype or development environments into qualified, controlled, repeatable production.
* Working knowledge of APQP per AS9145, AS9102 first article inspection, supplier quality, configuration management, CAPA, and risk based process control.
* Ability to influence senior technical leaders without defaulting to authority or unnecessary bureaucracy. Strong facilitation, coaching, and conflict resolution skills.
* Experience with customer and supplier quality requirements, quality metrics, and cross functional improvement programs.
* Ability to work on site in Denver and travel periodically to suppliers and other Red 6 locations.
* Must be US Citizen to have the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.

**Preferred Experience**

* ISO 45001 implementation or certification leadership; AS9115 awareness for deliverable software where relevant.
* DoD prime contractor interfaces, DCMA, DFARS, and applicable government customer quality requirements.
* Experience with PLM, MES, ERP, and integrated digital quality workflows, especially Windchill, Epsilon3, and Unanet.
* Lean Six Sigma, ASQ quality credentials, GD&T, hardware reliability, and complex electromechanical systems.
* Experience developing small teams into mature, business enabling quality organizations.

**What Success Looks Like In The First 12 Months**

* Publish an agreed risk based Quality maturity roadmap with clear process owners and milestones.
* Sustain AS9100 compliance and close systemic audit or corrective action gaps with evidence of effectiveness.
* Introduce an appropriate APQP and production readiness framework for priority product lines.
* Improve supplier quality visibility, product traceability, and readiness of controlled manufacturing documentation.
* Demonstrate stronger Quality–Engineering collaboration through earlier issue resolution and fewer late stage quality surprises.
* Provide leadership with a concise scorecard covering escapes, rework, supplier performance, CAPA aging, audit findings, and readiness milestones.

Estimated Base Salary range dependent on skills and experience: $175,000 to $195,000
  
  
**Full-Time Employee Benefits**

**Company & Job Overview**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Operations is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in Operations leadership, particularly in a medical device, medical technology or biotechnology organization. They will possess deep expertise in talent management, organizational development, and workforce planning.

This position is an office-based position at the company’s Irvine, CA headquarters.

* Translate corporate vision into actionable operational strategies, setting short- and long-term objectives for scaling manufacturing and supply chain.

We're looking for talented individuals who share our passion for excellence and innovation.
  
  
**Position Overview**
This role provides senior leadership and ownership of the functions that safeguard product integrity and the operating environment: Quality, Compliance (Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Safety and regulatory conformance), Security, and Facilities. The position is accountable for ensuring that products consistently meet quality specifications, that operations remain fully compliant with regulatory and safety standards, that the site and its products are secure, and that facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment. The role establishes clear metrics and ownership across these areas and reports performance to senior leadership.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Quality: Establish and maintain quality control protocols for raw materials, components, and finished products. Design inspection and testing processes and provide guidance on maintaining consistent quality from the beginning of production through final release. Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control teams, monitor quality metrics, and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate root causes of defects. Ensure conformance to customer, product, and industry specifications.
* Compliance: Ensure full compliance of operations with ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and applicable safety standards in accordance with New Jersey law. Own audits, certifications, and documentation, and serve as the primary liaison with regulatory bodies, auditors, and customers on compliance matters. Identify potential risks and pitfalls (e.g., equipment failures or other disruptions) and develop strategies to mitigate these issues through process improvement, alternative suppliers of materials, or altered equipment.
* Security: Oversee physical and product security programs consistent with the company's trust and authentication mission. Establish and enforce protocols to protect raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, and sensitive assets throughout the facility and supply chain. Ensure operations meet payment-industry and customer security requirements, and manage security personnel and access controls across all shifts.
* Accountability: Own the key performance indicators and reporting for quality, compliance, security, and facilities. Establish clear ownership, metrics, and dashboards, report performance to senior management, and foster a culture of accountability across the organization. Manage a team of approximately 35 people across 7 shifts supporting QA, Safety & Security.

records.description:
**About This Role**
The Head of Corporate Quality is responsible for creating and managing the Global Biogen Quality Management System (QMS). The main areas of focus include Quality Systems, internal and external audits for cGMP compliance (including external vendors and CMOs), IT Quality, Technical Product Complaints, and Central Knowledge Management (including documentation).
  
  
This role is central to Quality and PO&T, managing risk, compliance performance, staying compliant with regulatory changes, and seeking opportunities to gain efficiency and effectiveness in the administration of PO&T’s cGMP systems. Additionally, the role is accountable for preparing semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS and informing Executive Management of potential business risks due to a changing regulatory environment or systemic issues within the company. This role also serves as the principal liaison with the R&D Clinical Compliance organization and provides guidance for ICH conformance. Oversight includes biologic products, ASOs, small molecule products, gene therapy, devices, digital, and combination products.
  
  
*This role is hybrid- RTP or hybrid- Cambridge based.*
**Travel requirements**
: 25% – 50% depending on location. More travel required if not located in RTP.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Implement integrated quality systems, policies, and standards applicable to all Biogen U.S. and international manufacturing sites and PO&T locations, including Baar, Cambridge, Netherlands, Solothurn, and RTP.
* Develop and maintain a risk assessment process for evaluating and monitoring all cGXP systems.
* Ensure regulatory inspection responses are assessed holistically.
* Establish clear goals and effective metrics that provide insight into industry benchmarks and applicable trends regarding cGMP compliance.
* Oversee external monitoring of regulatory updates (domestic and international) and incorporate changes into Biogen’s QMS as needed.
* Internal and external GxP and ISO audit programs, including risk management and audit program oversight.
* Ensure Biogen’s internal manufacturing sites, Quality Systems, and vendors operate in a state of cGMP compliance, with any risks appropriately communicated and escalated.

**IT QA Department**

* Oversee GxP IT computerized systems across Biogen, including underlying infrastructure.
* Define appropriate standards and manage lifecycle documentation and supporting processes to ensure compliant implementation and management through retirement.

**Lifecycle Management**

* Oversee process and compliance-related content (specifically documentation, including governing policies, process documents, and other similar GxP documents) in the electronic document management system.
* Protect, index, classify, and archive GXP records, digitally preserve vital records, manage records lifecycle, and translate GMP content needed in multiple languages.
* Oversee the PO&T training program, providing global guidance and standards to ensure appropriate GxP training is conducted.

**Technical Product Complaint Department**

* Develop and maintain policies and procedures to manage complaints in line with industry and regulatory standards.
* Identify strategy and provide direction to team members regarding complaint investigation, root cause analysis, CAPAs, regulatory responses, and launch readiness for new products.
* Ensure trending and reporting of complaint cases and metrics, including appropriate escalation and response to significant events.

**Global Management Review (GMR)**

* Act as the chair for the GMR, ensuring ongoing management review and awareness of Biogen Quality and compliance performance (in accordance with cGMP and ICH expectations).
* Prepare semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS based on GMR outcomes.
* Establish short and long-term goals, objectives, and strategies for the Global Corporate Quality organization.
* Ensure appropriate policies and procedures are in place to measure, monitor, and report "actual" versus "planned" results.
* Drive major projects and programs for the Organizational Unit or Function to completion within schedule and budget.
* Manage multiple cost centers and determine the development of overall objectives and long-range goals of the organization.
* Interact directly with senior representatives of regulatory agencies, including the FDA and EMEA.
* Manage direct reports and managers of managers to increase their performance and effectiveness.

**Who You Are**
You are a seasoned leader in the pharmaceutical industry with an expert understanding of both U.S. and international regulatory requirements. Your influence within an organization is felt through consistent execution and strong leadership competencies. With excellent communication and change management skills, you're adept at leading and implementing change. You thrive in a highly regulated environment and have comprehensive knowledge of the pharmaceutical product development process.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Required Skills:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field with a minimum of 15 years of leadership experience in the pharmaceutical industry.
* Minimum of 10 years’ experience leading a Quality Assurance, Regulatory, or Corporate organization at the Director+ level in a highly regulated environment, preferably in biotech, pharmaceutical, or similar industry.
* Experience with the FDA, EMEA, and preferably multiple additional regulatory agencies in other foreign countries.
* Experience in clinical and commercial products as well as both large and small molecule programs, device, and combination products is strongly preferred. ASQ or other auditing certification is beneficial.
* Quality and Compliance experience consistent with worldwide regulatory requirements.
* Expert knowledge of US and International cGxPs, ISO, ICH, and Device regulations.

The Global Head of Quality provides strategic leadership and oversight of ProSciento's global Quality department, establishing the strategy, direction, governance, and priorities for the function. This role will oversee the Quality Management System (QMS) and ensures the organization maintains the highest standards of quality, regulatory compliance, and inspection readiness.

  

This role is accountable for establishing and advancing the company's quality strategy, Quality by Design and governance framework, and quality culture while ensuring compliance with applicable GxP regulations, FDA requirements, ISO standards, and other country specific, regional, and international regulatory requirements. The Global Head of Quality partners closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement, operational excellence, risk management, and organizational effectiveness while supporting ProSciento's strategic growth. Performs duties in accordance with ProSciento's values, policies, and procedures. Approximately 20% domestic and international travel is expected, with additional travel required based on business needs.

  

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

  

  
* Provides strategic leadership for ProSciento’s Quality department, establishing the vision, priorities, and organizational structure to support the company’s operations and business objectives.
  
* Accountable for the design, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with all applicable regulations including GCP, GLP, GMP (GxP), FDA, ISO, data privacy requirements, and other local, national, and international requirements.
  
* Responsible to oversee the quality of Global CRO studies and local site CRU trials as well as hands on experience implementing and maintaining a strategic Quality by Design framework for both business units.

* Oversee the development, maintenance, and governance of Quality Management System documentation, including quality policies, SOPs, work instructions, controlled documents, training programs, equipment records, and electronic document management systems.
  
* Partners with Information Technology and business leaders to ensure computerized systems, electronic records, and applicable equipment are appropriately qualified, verified, or validated in accordance with regulatory requirements and industry best practices.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

**QUALIFICATIONS & EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:**

  

**Qualifications:**

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  

  
* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, or Regulatory Compliance within the CRO or clinical research industry, including at least 5 years in senior quality leadership roles with responsibility for organizational quality strategy and personnel management with a minimum of 3 years of Global experience.
  
* Equivalent combinations of education, training, and relevant experience will be considered.
  

  

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND COMPETENCIES REQUIREMENTS:**

  

**Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:**

  

  
* Extensive knowledge of Quality Management Systems and quality governance, with demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and continuously improving quality systems within clinical research and regulated environments.
  
* Comprehensive knowledge of applicable global regulatory requirements and industry standards, including FDA regulations, ICH Guidelines, GCP, GLP, GMP (GxP), ISO 9001, data integrity, and applicable privacy requirements. Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and continuously improving Quality Management Systems (QMS) supporting GCP, GLP, GMP (GxP) environments and clinical research operations.
  
* Demonstrated experience leading regulatory inspections, sponsor and internal audits, supplier qualification programs, CAPA governance, inspection readiness, and enterprise quality risk management.
  
* Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing quality organizations, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  
* Proven strategic leadership, organizational planning, and change management skills, with the ability to partner with executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to establish quality strategies and organizational priorities.
  
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and risk assessment capabilities.
  
* Strong communication and executive presentation skills with the ability to influence stakeholders across all organizational levels.
  
* Experience leading regulatory inspections, sponsor interactions, and quality governance forums.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to interpret complex regulations, prepare executive reports, develop policies and procedures, and effectively communicate with regulatory agencies, sponsors, auditors, executive leadership, and employees.

**Job Summary**
The
**VP, Enterprise Quality**

Reporting to the SVP of Global Integrated Supply Chain, this role is responsible for defining the global quality strategy, establishing the enterprise quality management system, and driving quality excellence across all regions, SBUs, products, and manufacturing locations.
  
  
This leader will build global standards, governance, talent, and performance management systems across core elements of quality, including: quality control and assurance, supplier quality, APQP/PPAP, New Product Development (Design For Quality), early launch containment, warranty and field quality, customer experience feedback loops, and enterprise quality metrics.
  
  
This leader partners closely with Engineering, GISC functions, and customer‑facing teams such as Services and Field Operations to drive an integrated approach that connects customer experience, design intent, supplier performance, manufacturing execution, and lifecycle reliability.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
**Enterprise Quality Strategy & Governance**

* Establish and own the Enterprise Quality Strategy that sets the long‑term vision for enterprise quality excellence.

* Oversee global quality performance across the full value chain: suppliers, manufacturing, engineering, and aftermarket.

**Strengthen New Product Development (NPD) Quality**

* Partner with Engineering to embed quality into design through DFQ, risk assessment, and VOC integration.
* Establish robust Design for Quality (DFQ) practices and ensure quality requirements are integrated from concept through launch.
* Establish early launch containment and post‑launch learning loops.

**Improve Field Quality And Customer Experience**

* Create strong connections between customer complaints, service data, warranty analytics, and factory processes.
* Improve warranty performance and reduce related costs through systemic corrective action and predictive analytics.
* Establish global feedback loops that translate customer pain directly into engineering and manufacturing action.

* Champion quality as a core value that transcends job titles and is embraced across engineering, supply chain, operations, and field teams.
* Build a global, high‑performing enterprise quality organization, with clear roles across regions, SBUs, and plants.
* Strengthen quality competencies across inspection, problem‑solving, supplier quality, NPD quality, and digital quality.
* Establish a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.

Be a part of our mission. As a global climate innovator, sustainability and operational excellence are core to how we deliver value to our customers. You will build the foundations, capabilities, and standards necessary to reduce Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), strengthening new product development discipline, improve customer experience, and embed quality excellence across engineering, operations, supply chain, and field/service operations. If you are energized by building world‑class quality systems, driving measurable customer impact, and leading change across a global industrial enterprise — we invite you to boldly challenge what’s possible.
  
  
**What You Will Bring**

* Proven track record reducing COPQ, improving customer satisfaction, and building proactive quality cultures.

records.title: Head of Quality and Regulatory
records.description:
Cytovale, Inc. | South San Francisco, CA
  
  
**Reports to:**
Chief Operating Officer
  
  
**Function:**
Quality and Regulatory Compliance
  
  
**Location:**
**Bay area, onsite role**
**About Cytovale**
Cytovale is a medical diagnostics company focused on providing a faster, more insightful way to diagnose fast-moving and immune-mediated diseases. Cytovale's IntelliSep test is the first and only stand-alone sepsis detection assay to quickly and accurately analyze white blood cell structure to stratify a patient's risk of sepsis. The test simply and clearly shows risk of sepsis using a biomechanical evaluation of white blood cells from a standard blood draw, generating results in less than 10 minutes. For more information, please visit www.cytovale.com.
  
  
**Job Description**
The Head of Quality and Regulatory owns Cytovale's Quality Management System and serves as the company's designated Management Representative. This leader is accountable for the effectiveness and compliance of the QMS under FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, ISO 14971, and applicable IEC standards, and for the quality engineering capability that supports design change, process validation, and on-market product improvement for the IntelliSep system and its consumables.
  
  
The role is quality-first with a strong regulatory partnership. Working alongside the Senior Director of Regulatory Affairs, the Head of Quality and Regulatory shapes an 18- to 24-month regulatory roadmap spanning letters to file, Special and Traditional 510(k)s, and Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs), so that product and reliability improvements reach customers predictably and compliantly. The position leads all internal and external audits, third-party registrations, and agency inspections, and is expected to make the organization both more compliant and more nimble.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Quality Strategy and Leadership**

* Define and execute an enterprise Quality strategy that supports regulatory obligations, operational objectives, and long-term growth; establish annual quality objectives and the KPIs used to report progress to executive leadership.
* Lead a multidisciplinary Quality organization spanning Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering, Design Quality, Quality Systems, Process Validation, Incoming Inspection, and the audit program.
* Set the strategy for quality infrastructure, including eQMS evolution and the application of AI and analytics to quality processes.

**Quality Management System and Compliance**

* Serve as Management Representative; own the effectiveness of the QMS and its core processes, including CAPA, nonconformance and deviation management, complaint handling, change control, document control, training, and management review.
* Drive process improvements that allow the organization to move quickly while maintaining full FDA, ISO, and QMSR compliance, with documentation that is cohesive, consistent, and built on continuous-improvement principles.
* Establish and sustain a disciplined operating rhythm for internal audits, annual post-market reviews, and periodic management reviews.
* Maintain a proactive state of inspection readiness and lead the organization through FDA inspections, Notified Body audits, and third-party registration activities.

**Design Quality, Change Management, and Regulatory Roadmap**

* Direct design quality assurance across product development and design-change programs, allocating resources, managing budgets, and embedding quality engineers in project teams to ensure efficient, compliant execution.
* Partner with the Senior Director of Regulatory Affairs to develop and maintain a forward-looking 18- to 24-month regulatory roadmap covering letters to file, Special and Traditional 510(k)s, and PCCPs that enable feature and reliability improvements.
* Provide subject matter expertise in design of experiments, process validation, statistical methods, software validation, test method validation and measurement systems analysis, risk management and FMEA, and cybersecurity.

**Manufacturing, Supplier, and Product Quality**

* Own the Quality Improvement Plans for the IntelliSep instrument and associated consumables, and partner with Manufacturing and Engineering on qualification, process capability, and design-transfer activities.
* Govern manufacturing process changes with appropriate validation and documentation and ensure nonconformances are investigated and closed promptly.
* Direct the supplier quality program in collaboration with Supply Chain and R&D, including supplier selection and qualification, audits, performance monitoring, and supplier corrective actions.

**Post-Market Surveillance and Continuous Improvement**

* Own the post-market surveillance process end to end, from complaint intake through investigation, trending, product-improvement ticketing, and MDR and vigilance reporting.
* Monitor quality performance through data analysis and trend identification to surface risks early and prioritize improvement initiatives.
* Lead complex investigations and root-cause analyses; strengthen CAPA effectiveness and build organizational capability in structured problem solving.

**People and Culture**

* Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team of quality engineers, quality professionals, and future quality leaders; foster accountability, engagement, and ownership at every level.
* Champion a company-wide culture of quality through hands-on leadership, cross-functional partnership, and visible participation in QE and QMS activities.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering discipline.
* 10+ years of progressive quality leadership in the medical device or IVD industry, with 7+ years of experience managing quality teams and organizational performance.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Engineering serves as a core executive leader within PDTO, providing strategic, multi-disciplinary oversight across Xeris’s entire outsourced manufacturing, supply chain, and device engineering functions. Operating strictly within a contract manufacturing ecosystem, this executive leads four distinct functional pillars: Commercial Manufacturing & Supply Chain Logistics, Manufacturing Science & Technology (MS&T), Process Innovation & Life Cycle Management, and Device Development.
  
  
The primary mandate for this position is to ensure seamless integration and flawless execution across a highly diverse portfolio that spans small molecules, peptides, and biologics, in both oral solid and complex injectable dosage forms. The Vice President will guide products through the entire lifecycle continuum—from clinical development and process scale-up through commercial launch, combination product/device integration, and post-approval Life Cycle Management (LCM)—while ensuring uncompromising product quality and regulatory compliance.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

**Physical Requirements**
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
The work environment characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ.
  
  
As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success.
  
  
Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.
  
  
*Please note: This role will be based at Arsenal-01 in Columbus, OH. A successful candidate will be expected to work out of Columbus, OH. Based on eligibility, relocation assistance may be available. There will likely be 25% - 50% travel required for the role.*
**What You'll Do**

* First and foremost, deliver outcomes for the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization
* Create a clear vision for Manufacturing Operations

+ You are a key leader in supporting and strengthening the vision of AD&S Production
+ Manage the portfolio of projects necessary to achieve your vision for Manufacturing Operations

* Collaborate successfully with leaders across our production organization

+ Leaders include Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Planning, Quality, and Supply Chain

* Deliver quality products, on-time and at cost

+ Own attainment for both current and emerging programs

* Own the culture on the floor

+ Be a stakeholder in all programs, policies, etc. that affect life on the floor
+ Maximize for what’s right both for Anduril’s future and maintaining a strong team culture
+ Coach, mentor and support Manufacturing Operations Managers and Production Supervisors
+ Create and maintain a high bar for excellence

* Clearly communicate up and out

+ Provide consistent and high-quality briefs both up, to Anduril Senior Leadership, and out, to AD&S Customers

* In summary, show up every day with a high level of urgency, ownership, and enthusiasm to get the job done

**Required Qualifications**

* 6+ years experience managing manufacturing and production operations
* 3+ years in a supervisor or production operations management role at the Director level or above
* 3+ years of experience as a manager of managers
* Experience managing operator / technician workforce of 100+ within direct organization
* Experience working directly and communicating with designers and engineers
* A full understanding of the product life cycle (NPI to scaled production), LEAN manufacturing principles, and change management
* Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
* You have a passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor or Master’s degree in a technical field (engineering, business, or applied science)
* Working knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA laws

US Salary Range
  
  
$190,000—$252,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.

**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. **Data Privacy**

We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Director of Production to lead and evolve our global production organization within a fast-paced Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) environment. This role is critical in driving operational excellence across both domestic and international production, while also reimagining how production can be more innovative, automated, and scalable as the business grows.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who thrives in complexity, can manage a large SKU portfolio across multiple markets, builds strong global vendor partnerships, and inspires teams through coaching and mentorship. This person will lead on behalf of the department head when needed and serve as a strategic thought partner across the organization. We are open to candidates from a variety of industries, provided they bring transferable production leadership experience and a passion for continuous improvement.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Global Production Leadership & Strategy
  
  

* Lead end-to-end domestic and international production operations, with ownership of the full purchase order (PO) lifecycle from placement through manufacturing, delivery, and payment.
* Develop and execute production strategies that support growth, scalability, and on-time delivery across multiple regions and manufacturing partners.

Innovation & Automation
  
  

* Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and system enhancements to improve speed, visibility, and decision-making.

People Leadership & Development
  
  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing production team, fostering a culture of accountability, growth, and engagement.

* Develop future leaders through coaching, feedback, and development planning.

Operational Excellence & Scale
  
  

* Strengthen operational rigor through standardized workflows and clear cross-functional handoffs.
* Identify and proactively address risks related to capacity, cost, supply continuity, and execution across domestic and international production.
* Ensure production operations are scalable to support rapid growth and evolving business needs.

What You'll Bring

* Experience managing and developing teams of 5–10; a hands-on people leader with a passion for coaching, mentoring, and team development within a lean, high-output team structure.

* Track record of driving process improvement, innovation, and automation.

records.description:
****Panther: Better Health Is Skin Deep****
Panther is building the leading skin-powered treatment delivery and data platform for health and longevity. Its proprietary intradermal SmartPatch™ precisely delivers treatments to activate local and systemic healing, unlocking the skin as a scalable gateway for care. Panther’s AI-based platform accelerates partners’ product development and personalizes treatment, resulting in compelling consumer and provider experiences. Panther is targeting economically attractive markets of increasing clinical and regulatory difficulty, starting with its PIQUE™ branded Skincare products in mid-2027, and rapidly progressing to Medical Aesthetics and Therapeutics thereafter. Panther’s platform, significant IP portfolio and staged regulatory strategy provide a defensible moat. Panther is led by a team of successful entrepreneurs and operators and is advised by leading scientific experts.
  
  
**The Opportunity**
Panther Life Sciences is building a new category of consumer-centric health and beauty products powered by our SmartPatch platform. As we move from development into commercialization, manufacturing becomes the critical unlock for scale, quality, and customer trust.
  
  
We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing Operations to own this transition end-to-end. This role is responsible for translating innovative R&D into reliable, high-quality, and scalable commercial production across both cosmetic and medical device products. You will lead the build-out of Panther's manufacturing strategy, serving as the bridge between internal development teams and external CMO partners.
  
  
You will define how manufacturing operates at Panther, from selecting and standing up partners, to leading technology transfer, to building the systems that allow us to scale from thousands to millions of units. This is not a maintenance role. You will be building the manufacturing function from scratch. Your work will directly impact product availability, customer experience, and the company's ability to grow.
  
  
You will work closely with the leadership team and cross-functional team members in formulation, device development, and quality to establish a manufacturing engine that supports both near-term commercial goals and long-term platform expansion. This is for someone who wants to build, scale, and set the standard for manufacturing in a category-defining company with a great team and a platform that is already generating clinical results. If you want to build something that matters, we want to hear from you.
  
  
Some travel will required approximately 10% -30%
  
  
This role is ideally based in Pittsburgh, with New York as an alternative location."

records.description:
Director of Manufacturing

  
POSITION SUMMARY
  

Weaver Popcorn is seeking an experienced manufacturing leader to direct the
**Malden, Missouri**
operation and strengthen safety, quality, service, cost performance, throughput, and associate development. The Director of Manufacturing provides strategic and hands-on leadership for plant operations, maintenance, sanitation, scheduling, grower partnership, and continuous improvement while ensuring reliable execution of annual operating priorities.

  

This leader will establish clear performance expectations, develop plant leadership and frontline capability, optimize equipment and labor effectiveness, and partner across Quality, Field Operations, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, and Continuous Improvement to deliver sustainable operational and financial results.

  
HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?Manufacturing & Operational Leadership
  

  
* Lead the Malden manufacturing operation with accountability for safety, quality, service, cost, throughput, schedule attainment, sanitation, labor effectiveness, and overall plant performance.
  
* Establish clear operational standards, performance goals, equipment expectations, and operating cost objectives aligned with the annual plan.
  
* Drive reliable production output and efficient growth by ensuring the right equipment, staffing, operating systems, and performance measures are in place.
  
* Lead regular operating reviews with plant leadership to evaluate productivity, downtime, quality, staffing, schedule attainment, and corrective actions.
  
* Ensure manufacturing systems, procedures, and policies are consistently deployed, understood, and followed across assigned operations.
  
* Align internal manufacturing capabilities with customer needs, production schedules, raw-material availability, and growth expectations.
  

  
Safety, Quality & Food Manufacturing Compliance
  

  
* Provide visible leadership for a safe workplace and hold leaders accountable for proactive hazard identification, corrective action, training, and compliance.
  
* Partner closely with Quality leadership to ensure compliance with food safety and quality requirements, including HACCP, GMPs, sanitation standards, product controls, and applicable regulatory and customer requirements.
  
* Support disciplined investigation and sustainable corrective action for safety events, quality deviations, operational failures, customer concerns, and recurring performance issues.
  
* Ensure plant practices support audit readiness, traceability, sanitation effectiveness, and consistent production of safe, conforming product.
  
* Reinforce the authority and responsibility to stop or correct work when safety, food safety, quality, or regulatory requirements are not being met.
  

  
Continuous Improvement, Reliability & Capital
  

  
* Deploy Lean manufacturing, Statistical Process Control, and structured problem-solving methods to improve throughput, yield, reliability, labor efficiency, and cost performance.
  
* Identify operational failures and constraints, establish root causes, implement corrective actions, and verify sustained effectiveness.
  
* Develop and maintain meaningful manufacturing KPIs and equipment-efficiency measures that support timely, fact-based decisions.
  
* Partner with Maintenance and plant leaders to improve equipment reliability, preventive maintenance effectiveness, space utilization, and production capacity.
  
* Jointly establish capital expenditure priorities and lead effective execution of approved capital and process-improvement projects.
  
* Challenge existing practices, standardize successful improvements, and build continuous-improvement capability throughout the operation.
  

  
Grower, Supply Chain & Cross-Functional Partnership
  

  
* Collaborate with Field Operations to support grower relationships, contracted acreage plans, raw-material supply, and growth objectives.
  
* Partner with Supply Chain and plant scheduling teams to balance customer requirements, inventory, capacity, labor, and raw-material availability.
  
* Work with Finance and Information Technology to strengthen business processes, operating data, management reporting, budgeting, and decision-support tools.
  
* Contribute the manufacturing perspective to companywide initiatives led by Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, Quality, and other functional leaders.
  
* Communicate operational risks, priorities, tradeoffs, and performance clearly to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
  

  
People Leadership & Talent Development
  

  
* Lead, coach, and develop plant leaders and assigned functional leaders; establish clear goals, accountabilities, performance expectations, and development plans.
  
* Build a culture of excellence, ownership, accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement at every level of the operation.
  
* Develop internal talent, strengthen succession readiness, and partner with Human Resources to recruit and retain a capable workforce.
  
* Build associate competency through effective training, qualification, coaching, and skills-development programs.
  
* Use a visible, participative leadership style that communicates direction, listens for understanding, addresses conflict directly, and earns followership.
  

  
WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?
  

  
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Technology, Business, Operations Management, or a related field.
  
* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including at least 10 years in a Plant Manager or comparable senior manufacturing leadership role; food or agricultural processing experience strongly preferred.
  
* Demonstrated success applying Lean manufacturing, Statistical Process Control, root-cause analysis, and structured problem-solving methods to improve throughput, equipment efficiency, labor productivity, yield, and cost performance.
  
* Experience leading workplace safety, food manufacturing quality systems, sanitation, GMPs, HACCP-based programs, and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.
  
* Proven financial acumen, including budgeting, P&L accountability, capital prioritization, and analysis of manufacturing KPIs and cost drivers.
  
* Demonstrated success developing leaders, strengthening organizational capability, managing change, and building accountability in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
  
* Ability to travel regionally approximately 15% and remain available outside normal business hours when operational needs require support.
  

  
Preferred Qualifications
  

  
* Leadership experience in popcorn, corn, grain, ingredient, food processing, or a related agricultural manufacturing environment.
  
* Experience leading capital projects, technical teams, maintenance-reliability programs, and high-engagement employee relations.
  
* Formal training or certification in Lean, Six Sigma, safety, continuous improvement, or project leadership.
  
* Experience partnering directly with growers or agricultural supply networks.
  

  
WHERE & WHEN WILL YOU WORK?
  

This role operates across office, agricultural, warehouse, and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Manufacturing must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when safety, quality, customer, staffing, equipment, or other operational needs require support. Regional travel of approximately 15% is expected, with additional travel based on business needs.

  
WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?
  

  
* Strong, sustained performance in safety, quality, service, cost, throughput, schedule attainment, and customer satisfaction.
  
* Improved equipment reliability, operating efficiency, labor effectiveness, yield, and cost performance supported by clear KPIs.
  
* Consistent execution of manufacturing, sanitation, food safety, quality, and operating standards.
  
* Disciplined problem solving that reduces recurring failures and produces measurable, sustained improvement.
  
* A capable and accountable plant leadership team with clear goals, stronger bench strength, and active development plans.
  
* Effective partnership across Quality, Field Operations, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, and Continuous Improvement.
  
* Credible, visible leadership that builds ownership, engagement, and confidence throughout the Malden operation.
  

  
HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?
  

  
* Competitive compensation.
  
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
  
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
  
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
  
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.
  

  
EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
  

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

records.description:
**POSITION PURPOSE**

This position is responsible for leading, planning, organizing, and managing the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of the Bison Generation Station (BGS) facility to economically produce electricity to satisfy member needs.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

* Provide technical input for the decision-making process in power plant operation and maintenance. Keep plant staff informed of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of the facility and implement necessary corrective actions.
* Manage plant operational equipment; develop and maintain plant personnel and equipment safety standards; and develop preventative maintenance procedures and operational procedure manuals.
* Support the safety program by rigorously assuring standards are enforced and safety is at the forefront of all actions.
* Work in collaboration with other departments to build and adhere to all project budgets; responsible for developing and adhering to the BGS Long-Range Engineering Plan and the Capital Budget.
* Supervise the selection, training, development, and supervision of BGS employees.
* Evaluate the performance of plant section heads reporting to the position, review performance evaluations for all employees, and recommend salary adjustments for plant employees.
* Direct the development and submission of required reports to assure documentation and communication of plant operations, maintenance, and environmental activities.
* Authorize all plant purchase request orders and staff timesheets. In addition, review all proposed changes or modifications to plant systems or equipment and proposed tests or research programs.
* Responsible for staff development to ensure that each section functions safely and efficiently and that they all work together to meet the goals and objectives of Basin Electric, the plant operations division, and the station.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Energy Management, Business, or an Engineering Accreditation Commission/ Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (EAC/ABET) accredited engineering program; and 10 years of related power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance, or engineering experience; or
* An associate’s degree in Power/Process Plan Technology or related field; and 12 years’ experience in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering; or
* A high school diploma or equivalent (GED or HSED); and 14 years’ in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering.
* Prior supervisory experience.
* A valid driver’s license.

**PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS**

This position requires constant sitting; and occasional lifting/carrying up to 50 pounds, pushing/pulling up to 20 pounds, standing, walking, bending, crawling, reaching, and climbing. This position uses office equipment and field tools. This position also requires finger dexterity, good vision/hearing, hand coordination, and the ability to perform close work, analyze data/reports, conduct research, and implement recommendations. This position occasionally works in areas of dirt/dust, fumes, chemicals, extreme heat/cold, vibration, noise, and poor ventilation. This position must be respirator qualified.

**KEY SKILLS**

* Effective administrative and human relation skills.
* Excellent organizational, written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficient with personal computers and Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Able to provide work direction, develop plans/procedures/goals, and present information to others.

**A ROLE THAT SUPPORTS YOUR CAREER AND YOUR FUTURE**

* Competitive salary aligned with experience.
* Relocation package to support your transition.
* Up to 15% 401(k) match.
* More benefits to support you.

Applicants interested in this opening should go to careers.basinelectric.com to apply. Employees must apply through Careers in SAP SuccessFactors.

The Signal Hill power plant is strategically located in Wichita County, Texas, near the rapidly expanding Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area. This 77 MW electric power generation facility utilizes GE gas combustion turbines, along with associated heat recovery steam generators and an ABB steam generator. Signal Hill plays a critical role in supplying power to the ERCOT market during periods of peak demand and supply volatility. The facility was honored with the 2014 Certificate of Recognition by the City of Wichita Falls, Texas, for its outstanding achievements in environmental excellence, including pollution prevention, waste minimization, and water conservation.
  
  
We are seeking an experienced and dedicated Plant Manager to oversee the operations of the Signal Hill power plant. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in power plant management and a commitment to operational excellence, safety, and environmental stewardship. As Plant Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the facility, while maintaining compliance with all regulatory requirements.

* Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, and safety regulations, and promote a culture of safety and environmental responsibility.
* Monitor plant performance and implement strategies to optimize efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness.
* Coordinate with ERCOT and other stakeholders to ensure the plant meets market demands during peak periods and supply volatility.
* Develop and manage the plant's budget, including forecasting and controlling operational costs.
* Lead and mentor a team of Plant Technicians, fostering a collaborative and high-performance work environment.
* Identify opportunities for continuous improvement in plant operations, maintenance practices, and environmental performance.
* Maintain strong relationships with local authorities, regulatory agencies, and the community.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant power industry experience, such as experience as a Power Plant Manager or in a comparable power generation leadership role, in lieu of a degree.
* Proven experience in power plant management, with a strong understanding of gas turbine and steam generator operations.
* Comprehensive knowledge of ERCOT market operations and regulatory requirements.
* Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to manage and motivate a diverse team.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, and operational excellence.
